newsitem.title: USA: Attorneys open New York coma rape trial.
newsitem.headline: Attorneys open New York coma rape trial.

text.p: Prosecutors on Friday opened the trial of a nursing home aide accused of raping a comatose patient who later gave birth, saying that genetic evidence would prove the identity of the rapist.

The public defender representing alleged attacker John Horace asked the 12-member jury to question the veracity of DNA testing and claimed that the accused man did not have the opportunity to rape the woman.

The woman, now 30, remains in a coma, as she has been since an automobile accident 11 years ago in upstate New York while she was a student at Cornell University in Ithaca. Her mother is raising the baby boy, now almost 11 months old.

Prosecutors say Horace, 53, raped the woman in August 1995 when he was a nursing assistant at the Westfall Health Care Facility in Brighton, New York, and she was a patient there. He is charged with rape and sexual abuse.

"She can't testify, but when John Horace had sexual intercourse with Jane Doe, little did he know that the seed he sowed that day would be the building block of a genetic witness that would identify him as Jane Doe's attacker," assistant state attorney general Jerry Solomon said in the prosecution's opening argument.

Solomon said DNA evidence shows a more-than-99 percent probability that Horace is the baby's father. DNA or deoxyribonucleic acid is a long, double-stranded molecule that is the main constituent of the chromosome and carries the genes along its strands.
Authorities tested Horace's blood and saliva from an envelope he licked and compared the evidence with amniotic fluid from the woman's womb and with the baby's blood.
In her opening argument, assistant public defender Yolanda Villa told the jury that the rape might have happened either before or after Horace's six-week tenure at the centre.
"Listen very carefully to whether you hear any evidence of John Horace's conduct at the Westfall nursing home during that period that is evidence of guilt. I submit there is none," Villa said.

Horace has served prison time for two other sex crimes. He pleaded guilty last year to impersonating a physician at an unlicensed "sex therapy clinic" and was convicted of fondling a 49-year-old multiple sclerosis patient, also at Westfall.
Jurors are not expected to be told about those cases unless he testifies in his own defence. If convicted, Horace faces a maximum prison sentence of eight-and-a-half to 25 years in prison.
